newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crude trade highlighted by Cusiana sale.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crude trade highlighted by Cusiana sale.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude trade on Monday was highlighted by a Cusiana sale at a higher-than-expected price, traders said.
Equity producer British Petroleum sold a cargo loading September 3-7 to a U.S. refiner at 57 cents a barrel under October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
This was the second Cusiana cargo to find a home in September. Last week, another U.S. refiner picked up a cargo from Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol at October WTI minus 65 cents a barrel.
The Cusiana loading program for September, which came out late Friday night, comprises 14-15 cargoes, up four to five from the August program.
Equity producers BP and Total have five and two cargoes, respectively, while Ecopetrol has the balance, including a cross-month cargo loading September 29 to October 3.
The sweet grade has been fetching higher prices lately partly as a result of the narrow trans-Atlantic arbitrage.
The September spread between Brent and WTI was around $1.35-1.40 a barrel on Monday afternoon, up from $1.20-1.30 a barrel late on Friday but still considered slim enough to discourage most sellers.
Nonetheless, at least two companies were tentatively showing the North Sea benchmark to U.S. buyers, asking around 20-25 cents a barrel under October WTI for mid-September delivery.
Meanwhile, a few stragglers of Nigerian crude were still looking for buyers in the second half of August, traders said.
Qua Iboe and Bonny Light were on offer around Dated Brent plus $1.80 a barrel, while Brass River was at $1.95 a barrel.
The sellers have knocked off about 10 cents a barrel since last week in response to tepid demand, traders said.
Among other foreign crudes on offer in the U.S. Gulf, a European company was offering Colombian Cano Limon for end-September delivery, asking October WTI minus $2.30 a barrel.
